transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-19
Time: 08:00 PST (16:00 UTC)
Duration: 62 minutes
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20260219-sputnik
Attendees:
 - Maya Chen (Redwood AE)
 - Omar Singh (Redwood SE)
 - Lena Park (Redwood Solutions Eng)
 - Rajesh Rao (Sputnik Head of ML)
 - Emily Torres (Product)
 - Marcus Li (SRE)
 - Sofia Alvarez (Security)

Summary:
Quick sync to define POC acceptance criteria for Sputnik's customer-facing summarization feature. Focus: golden prompts, regression suite, hallucination checks, scoring rubric, throughput targets and timeline for a 3-week pilot. Agreed artifacts: golden prompt spreadsheet, regression matrix, load slices, and security packet.

Topics:
- Success criteria and pass/fail gates
- Workload sizing and concurrency targets
- Benchmark plan (latency p50/p95, token cost)
- Quality checks: hallucination, format, factuality
- Scoring approach and thresholds
- Timeline and deliverables

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, thanks everyone for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood, I have Omar and Lena with me. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Rajesh Rao: Rajesh here.
[00:07] Emily Torres: Emily.
[00:08] Marcus Li: Marcus.
[00:09] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia on security.
[00:11] Maya Chen: Great. We want to use this 60-minute slot to get really specific on what success looks like for the POC, and what datasets / golden prompts you can give us. We're aiming for a 3-week pilot, is that still your target?
[00:23] Rajesh Rao: Yes, three weeks is what product wants. We want to make a decision based on quality and cost per 1k tokens, and also the hallucination profile — basically we need to be confident it won't invent contact details or medical advice.
[00:35] Omar Singh: Yep, understood. A couple quick clarifying Qs: when you say hallucination profile — do you have labeled examples of hallucination false positives or is this a manual label task for the POC?
[00:46] Rajesh Rao: We have about 200 labeled failures from our current LLM that we can share; plus we'd like you to run a set of 500 production-like prompts.
[00:55] Lena Park: Cool. For the golden prompts — we usually ask for 30-50 representative prompts that are high-signal plus a few edge cases. We'll create a golden prompt spreadsheet with columns: prompt, expected output (exact match or scoring hints), failure modes, and tolerance. Does that match what you had in mind?
[01:12] Emily Torres: That sounds right. Product wants both exact-format outputs (like JSON payloads for our UI) and loose summaries. The format checks are critical — if the model outputs malformed JSON we have to reject.
[01:23] Marcus Li: On the infra side, we need to know expected concurrency; currently our front end will hit the API at peak 60 rps during certain events, average 12 rps.
[01:32] Omar Singh: 60 rps peak — ok that helps. For the POC we typically run three load slices: baseline (avg 12 rps), peak (60 rps), and burst (120 rps) to see graceful degradation and fallback. We can run the baseline on Redwood Hosted and the peak on a small Dedicated pool to mimic production.
[01:48] Rajesh Rao: Quick Q on data handling — we can't have any prompt retention, and anything logged must be encrypted with our KMS.
[01:54] Sofia Alvarez: Yes that's a hard requirement; we have a list of legal/regulatory controls: SSO, SAML, audit logs, retention 0 days for prompts, and HSM-backed keying.
[02:03] Maya Chen: Understood. Our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and can be air-gapped; for the hosted POC we can configure ephemeral retention and route logs to your KMS-backed storage. We'll send the security packet.
[02:15] Sofia Alvarez: Please include SOC 2 type II, ISO, and the KMS architecture diagram.
[02:20] Lena Park: Back to quality, we propose the following scoring approach: for each golden prompt we compute a composite score made of 3 components — format (binary pass/fail), factuality (0-1), and hallucination penalty (0-1). Composite score = 0.5*format + 0.3*factuality + 0.2*(1 - hallucination_penalty). Threshold for POC success: composite >= 0.78 for 85% of golden prompts. Does that sound reasonable?
[02:44] Rajesh Rao: The weighting seems fine, but product insists on stricter format gating for schema outputs — format must be 100% for any prompt flagged as strict-schema.
[02:52] Maya Chen: We can add a strict-schema requirement: any prompt labeled strict-schema must have format pass in 100% of cases. We'll add that to the rubric.
[02:59] Emily Torres: Also we want per-prompt tolerances — e.g., numeric rounding allowed +-2% for amounts.
[03:06] Omar Singh: Good call. Our golden prompt template will include a tolerance column. For regression tests, we recommend 3 buckets: golden (30-50 prompts), regression (200 historical failure cases), and wildcards (500 production-like prompts). We'll run automatic scoring and then human review for borderline cases.
[03:24] Rajesh Rao: On hallucinations, what automated checks do you run? We need to detect invented entities and dates, and any output that references internal doc ids.
[03:33] Lena Park: We use a combination of string matching against allowed entity lists, a factuality classifier, and heuristics that detect improbable tokens (like phone numbers that don't match country codes). But to be honest, the classifier isn't perfect; so we pair it with spot human evaluation for the 5% worst-scoring outputs.
[03:49] Marcus Li: For the benchmarks — latency p50 target is <=120ms for baseline prompts, p95 <=350ms; during peak we allow p95 up to 700ms but we want graceful fallback. Token cost target is <= $0.90 per 1k tokens equivalent for the model profile we expect.
[04:08] Omar Singh: That aligns with our guidance. We'll run token-level cost reporting and show the trade-off between quantized model variants and latency. We may recommend a lower-precision quantized variant for cost-sensitive flows.
[04:20] Rajesh Rao: We also need to test KV cache hit scenarios because many requests will be follow-ups where cached context can reduce cost and latency.
[04:28] Omar Singh: Good call — we'll include KV/prefix cache tests: cold-start vs warmed cache, both single-turn and multi-turn contexts.
[04:34] Emily Torres: On scoring, can we get a dashboard that shows per-prompt pass/fail and an aggregated SLA-like report?
[04:41] Lena Park: Yes — we'll provide a per-prompt table, composite distribution, and an overall green/yellow/red pass band for the batch. We'll also attach the regression spreadsheet.
[04:49] Sophia (sic): [intended Sofia] One more security note: if you're sending sample prompts, ensure they are pseudonymized; we can't share PHI.
[04:56] Rajesh Rao: We'll scrub PHI and send synthetic where needed.
[05:00] Maya Chen: Great. Timeline proposal: Week 0 (this week) — share golden prompt template and security docs. Week 1 — customer provides dataset (500 prompts + 200 labeled failures). Week 2 — Redwood runs quality eval and initial load tests. Week 3 — final run, handoff and decision. Is that acceptable?
[05:18] Rajesh Rao: Yes. We may need an extra week for internal sign-off but we'll try to keep to 3.
[05:22] Marcus Li: On the infra bucket, if you need Dedicated pool we'll need pricing for a small GPU cluster for the week of the benchmark.
[05:30] Maya Chen: I'll send a pilot pricing sheet. For Dedicated, we have a small reserved for POC that keeps cost predictable — I'll include cost per hour and estimated token cost for the load slices.
[05:40] Emily Torres: For acceptance criteria, can you summarize the hard gates?
[05:44] Lena Park: Sure — proposed hard gates:
 - Strict-schema prompts must have 100% format pass.
 - Composite score >= 0.78 for 85% of golden prompts.
 - Regression false-positive rate <= 5% on the 200 known failures.
 - Latency p95 under 350ms for baseline slice; during peak p95 under 700ms with graceful fallback enabled.
 - No prompt retention; all logs encrypted with customer KMS.

[06:12] Rajesh Rao: If we hit all gates except one (say latency), do you offer mitigation like autoscale or fallbacks to cheaper model variants?
[06:20] Omar Singh: Yes, we can configure automatic fallback to a lower-latency variant or route to Dedicated nodes; we'll show a canary rollout and fallback policy in the runbook.
[06:29] Emily Torres: How will we measure hallucination penalty numerically?
[06:33] Lena Park: We'll count hallucination occurrences per output and normalize by token length, combine with classifier score. The penalty will be 0 for no hallucination and up to 1 for severe fabrications. We'll include examples in the rubric so it's reproducible.
[06:47] Maya Chen: Quick note — pls expect some transcription artifacts in our auto notes, but we will send the final rubric doc as a spreadsheet. Link placeholder: drive.google.com/sputnik-poc/golden-prompts (we'll actually share after the call).
[06:59] Rajesh Rao: Perfect. Security: Sofia will validate the SOC2 doc and KMS integration.
[07:04] Sofia Alvarez: Yep, I'll review and confirm by Thursday.
[07:08] Marcus Li: On the load test environment, we need to schedule an hour window to avoid interference with our staging jobs. Week of 3/2 we have Tuesday/Thursday open.
[07:17] Omar Singh: We'll tentatively target Tuesday 2026-03-03 for peak/burst tests. I'll send a calendar invite once we coordinate pricing and the Dedicated pool.
[07:26] Emily Torres: One operational ask — can the evaluation run produce a CSV export of per-prompt outputs for our SRE and product?
[07:33] Lena Park: Absolutely, CSV/JSON exports available along with annotated scores.
[07:37] Maya Chen: Ok let's do a quick recap and owner-level next steps.
[07:40] Maya Chen: Action items recap — Omar will draft the regression matrix and share the scoring spreadsheet by 2/23; Rajesh will provide the 500 prompts + 200 labeled failures by 2/24; Maya will send pricing and pilot contract by tomorrow 2/20; Sofia will pull SOC2 and KMS details by 2/25.
[07:58] Rajesh Rao: That matches expectations.
[08:00] Maya Chen: Any last questions?
[08:02] Emily Torres: Not from product.
[08:03] Marcus Li: No.
[08:04] Sofia Alvarez: None.
[08:05] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the golden prompt template and the security packet. Expect calendar invites for the benchmark windows.
[08:12] Rajesh Rao: Thanks.

Post-call notes:
- Shared artifacts to attach: golden-prompts-template.csv, scoring-rubric.xlsx, regression-matrix.csv, security-packet.pdf, pilot-pricing.pdf (links will be provided).
- Benchmarks planned: baseline/peak/burst with KV cache cold/warm slices.

Decision criteria (restated):
- Composite scoring RUBRIC with strict-schema gate as above.
- Operational acceptance if cost+latency within target and security controls validated.

End of transcript.
